summary: Find the starting station index from which a circular trip is possible, or -1.
mainInsight: If total gas < total cost there is no solution. Otherwise scan once keeping the tank; whenever it drops below 0 at station i, no station between the current start and i can be the start, so reset the tank and set start = i + 1. The final start is the answer.

cards.answer: One-pass greedy: no answer if total gas is below total cost; otherwise reset the start whenever the tank goes negative. Clue: On a circular route, running dry at station i rules out every start between the previous start and i, and a total shortfall rules out all starts, so one pass with a reset suffices.

promptVariants: Why can stations before the failing point be skipped, and why is total >= 0 enough?
What is the role of the total check?
cards.answer: If you start at s and run out of gas at i, any start in (s, i] arrives at i with no more gas than starting at s (the prefix before it was non-negative), so they also fail. If total gas >= total cost, the unique candidate after the last reset can complete the circle because the deficit before it is covered by the surplus after it.
cards.explanation: The solution is unique when it exists.

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def canCompleteCircuit(self, gas: List[int], cost: List[int]) -> int:
        if sum(gas) < sum(cost):                 # not enough fuel around the whole circle
            return -1
        start = tank = 0
        for i in range(len(gas)):
            tank += gas[i] - cost[i]
            if tank < 0:                         # cannot reach i + 1 from any start in [start, i]
                start = i + 1
                tank = 0
        return start
